Not set yet. Tap “Choose”, start at /sdcard and open folders until you reach the one with your images
The whole storage — nearly every photo on the phone will move
Data root of all apps — open one more level and pick the app you want
Starting from /sdcard, drill down to the exact image folder — that is the safest
Moves images from every level under the source folder
; note the target folder is inside the source, so files just moved there will be picked up as source again
Only moves images directly in the source folder, subfolders are ignored (safer when the target is inside the source)
Blank = no limit; skips old photos and thumbnails
Put it under DCIM or Pictures so the gallery sees it
Keeps the originals, adds a copy
{app} = source app name; blank = keep original
The name becomes a 15-character code; the same photo always gets the same name, so nothing is stored twice
Off: the target keeps the original name and only gets the suffix you set
Just a name so you can tell your rules apart.
Where the images to move are. The exact image folder is safest; picking the whole storage moves almost every photo.
When on, images in every subfolder below the source are moved too; off means only the top folder.
Only used with subfolders on: how many levels below the source to scan, 1 = the source folder only. Blank = all levels.
Only images changed in the last N days are moved; older ones stay. Blank = no limit.
Images smaller than N KB are skipped — handy for thumbnails and stickers. Exactly N KB is moved.
Where the images go. Keep it under DCIM or Pictures so the gallery can see them.
When on, each app\'s images go into a subfolder named after the app, e.g. DCIM/Qidian/…, so they do not mix.
Move: the original leaves its place. Copy: the original stays and the target gets a copy.
This is only a fallback: a change is usually moved within about 15 seconds. It sets the longest wait before a forced scan, not how often the folder is checked.
Added to the file name in the target. {app} becomes the source app name; blank keeps the original.
The new name is a 15-character code made from the content, so the same photo always gets the same name and is never stored twice.
Only files with these extensions are moved, separated by commas, e.g. jpg,png. Keep at least one, or nothing moves.
Counts how many images would move and roughly how much space they take. No file is touched.

Reuse this setup in one tap next time you create a rule

Your source is %1$s and the target %2$s is inside it. Files already moved will not be moved again (the app skips the target folder automatically), but it is clearer and easier to undo if you put the target outside the source. Save it this way anyway?

You picked /sdcard (the whole phone storage) as the source. After saving, nearly every image on the phone will be moved by this rule (in Move mode the originals leave their place). If you only want to tidy up one app, go back and open Android/data/<package>/… and pick a folder inside.
